obligation: Card brand notice: Visa account data compromise
citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised, Visa Supplemental Requirements v10.0 (effective 2026-06-25), Section A.1 to A.4
trigger: Evidence sufficient to raise a reasonable suspicion of, or to confirm, unauthorized access to Visa payment account data or to a system that stores, processes, or transmits it
deadline: Report to Visa within 3 calendar days of suspicion or confirmation; incident report within 3 calendar days after notifying Visa; at-risk account numbers within 3 calendar days of discovery, of Visa's request, or of setting the window of exposure
notify: Visa Global Risk Investigations (through the sponsor banks); acquiring banks immediately (Section A.3.1)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the company stores, processes, and transmits Visa account data for all three sponsor bank programs

obligation: Other card brands: American Express verified; Mastercard and Discover not verified (contractual)
citation: American Express Data Security Operating Policy (DSOP), United States, April 2026, Section 3. Mastercard and Discover rules, applied through the sponsor banks (Banks A, B and C), not verified: Mastercard's site returned HTTP 403 and no Discover rules page was found. Not law
trigger: Suspected or confirmed compromise of American Express, Mastercard or Discover card data (for American Express, a potential or confirmed compromise is a Data Incident)
deadline: American Express: immediately, and no later than 72 hours after discovery; then investigate, and engage a PCI Forensic Investigator within 5 days of discovery if 10,000 or more card numbers are involved (DSOP Section 3). Mastercard and Discover: per the sponsor banks's instructions (not verified)
notify: American Express Enterprise Incident Response Program (EIRP@aexp.com, 1-888-732-3750), with a named company contact; Mastercard and Discover through the sponsor banks (Banks A, B and C)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: Sponsor bank notice of suspected account data compromise (Banks A, B, C)
citation: Sponsor agreements (contract); Visa WTDIC v10.0 Section A.3.1
trigger: Suspected or confirmed account data compromise
deadline: Immediately (Visa); no later than 24 hours under each sponsor agreement
notify: Each bank's designated security and compliance contacts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all three banks

obligation: Bank service provider notification to Bank A (OCC)
trigger: Computer-security incident that has materially disrupted or degraded, or is reasonably likely to materially disrupt or degrade, covered services to the bank for four or more hours. Covered services here: authorization processing, clearing, settlement, reconciliation, and merchant funding files (sponsor agreement; 12 U.S.C. 1867(c)). Excludes previously communicated maintenance, testing, or updates (53.4(b))
deadline: As soon as possible after the determination
notify: At least one bank-designated point of contact; if none on file, the bank's CEO and CIO or two individuals of comparable responsibility (53.4(a)(2))
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - bank service provider to Bank A
clock_starts: Company's determination that the 4-hour threshold is met or reasonably likely
owner: Chief Compliance Officer with the incident commander

obligation: Bank service provider notification to Bank B (FDIC)
trigger: Same trigger as 53.4 for covered services to an FDIC-supervised institution
deadline: As soon as possible after the determination
notify: Bank B's designated points of contact (fallback: CEO and CIO, 304.24(a)(2))
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - bank service provider to Bank B (Integrated Payments program)
owner: Chief Compliance Officer with the incident commander

obligation: Bank service provider notification to Bank C (Federal Reserve)
trigger: Same trigger as 53.4 for covered services to a Board-supervised banking organization (Bank C is a state member bank)
deadline: As soon as possible after the determination
notify: Bank C's designated points of contact (fallback: CEO and CIO, 225.303(a)(2)). Contacts to be loaded by 2026-10-31 (POAM-007)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - bank service provider to Bank C (enterprise merchants and payouts settlement)
owner: Chief Compliance Officer with the incident commander

obligation: Banking organization notification incident (the banks' own duty)
trigger: Notification incident at a banking organization
deadline: No later than 36 hours after the bank determines a notification incident occurred
notify: Each bank's primary federal regulator (by the bank)
applies_at_this_tier: No - applies to the banks, not the company. The company's prompt notice gives each bank what it needs for its own decision

obligation: FTC Safeguards Rule notification event
trigger: Acquisition of unencrypted customer information without the individual's authorization (unauthorized access presumed to be acquisition absent reliable evidence otherwise) involving the information of at least 500 consumers
deadline: As soon as possible and no later than 30 days after discovery (first day known to any employee, officer, or agent other than the person committing the breach)
notify: Federal Trade Commission, through the electronic form on ftc.gov
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - financial institution under 16 CFR 314. Affected cardholders are counted toward the 500 (conservative reading; counsel confirms)

obligation: FTC notice law enforcement delay
trigger: A law enforcement official provides a written determination that public notice would impede a criminal investigation or damage national security
deadline: Initial delay of up to 30 days after notice to the FTC; up to 60 more days on written request; further delay only if FTC staff agrees
notify: Include in the FTC notice; FTC contacts the official
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if requested

obligation: NYDFS notice of cybersecurity incident (payouts subsidiary)
trigger: A cybersecurity incident at the covered entity, its affiliates, or a third-party service provider: one that requires notice to a government body, has a reasonable likelihood of materially harming a material part of the covered entity's normal operations, or deploys ransomware within a material part of its information systems
deadline: As promptly as possible and no later than 72 hours after determining that a cybersecurity incident has occurred
notify: NYDFS superintendent, electronically through the department's portal
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Cris Santos Payouts, LLC is a covered entity that runs on the parent's shared systems; incidents at the parent (an affiliate) count
clock_starts: Determination that a cybersecurity incident occurred

obligation: NYDFS updates after the incident notice
trigger: Material changes or new information after the 72-hour notice
deadline: Promptly; continuing obligation; provide any information NYDFS requests
notify: NYDFS superintendent
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: NYDFS notice and explanation of an extortion payment
trigger: Extortion payment made in connection with a cybersecurity event involving the covered entity
deadline: Notice within 24 hours of the payment; written explanation within 30 days (reasons, alternatives considered, diligence, and OFAC compliance diligence)
notify: NYDFS superintendent, electronically
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if any payment is made (POL-03 4.8 requires CEO, General Counsel, and insurer approval first)

obligation: SEC materiality determination
trigger: Cybersecurity incident discovered that could be material
deadline: Without unreasonable delay after discovery (the disclosure committee convenes within 48 hours under POL-03 4.4)
notify: Disclosure committee (General Counsel chairs); record the date and time of the determination
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - SEC registrant

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05 filing
trigger: Registrant determines a cybersecurity incident is material
deadline: Within 4 business days after the materiality determination
notify: SEC (public filing): material aspects of the nature, scope, and timing, and the material impact or reasonably likely material impact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - SEC registrant

obligation: SEC filing delay on Attorney General determination
trigger: U.S. Attorney General determines disclosure poses a substantial risk to national security or public safety and notifies the SEC in writing
deadline: Up to 30 days after the original due date; up to 30 more days on a further determination; in extraordinary circumstances a final period of up to 60 days (national security only)
notify: Department of Justice (through outside counsel); SEC notified by the Attorney General
applies_at_this_tier: Only if the Attorney General so determines

obligation: SEC annual cybersecurity disclosure
trigger: Annual report on Form 10-K
deadline: With the next Form 10-K; update the description of processes and any material effects of incidents
notify: SEC (Form 10-K)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - SEC registrant

obligation: Insider trading blackout
trigger: Disclosure committee convenes on a possibly material incident
deadline: Same day the committee convenes
notify: Committee members, incident responders with knowledge, and executives (special blackout notice)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - company policy, not a regulatory deadline

obligation: State breach notice to individuals (each state of residence)
citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information of residents where the company owns the data (for example merchant owner or workforce data); definitions vary by state
deadline: Varies by state; plan to the shortest
notify: Affected residents
applies_at_this_tier: Yes where the company is the data owner and the stolen elements meet the state's definition
clock_starts: Each state's trigger (often determination of breach)

obligation: State third-party agent notice to data owners (merchants)
trigger: Breach of a system the company maintains for merchants that involves personal information as each state defines it
deadline: Varies by state (Florida worked example: 10 days)
notify: Each affected merchant, with the information it needs for its own notices
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the company is a third-party agent for its merchants' cardholder data

obligation: State attorney general or regulator notice
trigger: Breach above a state-set count of residents, where the company is the data owner
deadline: Varies by state
notify: State attorneys general or regulators
applies_at_this_tier: Yes where thresholds are met

obligation: State consumer reporting agency notice
trigger: Notices above a state-set count
deadline: Varies by state
notify: Nationwide consumer reporting agencies
applies_at_this_tier: Yes where thresholds are met

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice to merchants (worked example)
trigger: Breach of security of a system the company maintains for merchants (covered entities) involving personal information of Florida residents; for card data, personal information means name plus card number with any required security code (501.171(1)(g))
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, no later than 10 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred
notify: Each affected merchant, with all information it needs for its notices; the company may send notices for the merchant (501.171(6)(b))
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - when the stolen elements meet the Florida definition
clock_starts: Determination of breach or reason to believe

obligation: Florida notice to individuals (worked example)
trigger: Breach of personal information of Florida residents where the company is the covered entity, or when sending notices for a merchant
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred (15 more days with good cause given in writing to the department)
notify: Affected Florida residents
applies_at_this_tier: Yes when the company owns the data or sends notices for a merchant
clock_starts: Determination of breach or reason to believe

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs (worked example)
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida, where the company is the covered entity
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred (no extension for this notice)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents and the company is the covered entity (otherwise the merchant's duty)
clock_starts: Determination of breach or reason to believe

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies (worked example)
trigger: Notice to more than 1,000 individuals at one time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if more than 1,000 individuals are notified

obligation: Florida no-notice determination (worked example)
trigger: After investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the covered entity reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Written determination kept at least 5 years; provided to the department within 30 days after the determination
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs
applies_at_this_tier: Only if that determination is made

obligation: Merchant, ISV partner, and enterprise merchant contract notices
citation: Merchant agreements; ISV partner agreements; enterprise merchant agreements (contract)
trigger: Security incident affecting merchant or cardholder data, or service availability
deadline: Per each agreement
notify: Affected merchants and partners; enterprise merchants' security contacts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal

obligation: SOC 1 and SOC 2 user entity communications
citation: Service commitments in SOC 1 and SOC 2 system descriptions (contract)
trigger: Incident that affects commitments described to user entities
deadline: Per the commitments; disclosed in the next report if within the period
notify: User entities (sponsor banks, enterprise merchants, ISV partners)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes
owner: Chief Compliance Officer with the service line owners

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom or extortion payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering any ransom or extortion payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if an extortion demand is made

obligation: Voluntary law enforcement report
trigger: Criminal compromise of payment data or ransomware
deadline: As soon as practicable; coordinate with counsel and the PFI
notify: FBI field office or IC3; U.S. Secret Service field office
applies_at_this_tier: Recommended

obligation: Cyber insurance claim notice
trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy; call the breach hotline before hiring vendors
notify: Carrier breach hotline (tower of $150 million)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports (pending final rule)
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment by a covered entity
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours (ransom payment). Not yet effective
notify: CISA
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; recheck when final

obligation: SCI event notification
trigger: SCI event at an SCI entity
deadline: Immediately; written notice within 24 hours
notify: SEC
applies_at_this_tier: No - not an SCI entity

obligation: Credit union reportable cyber incident
trigger: Reportable cyber incident at a federally insured credit union
deadline: No later than 72 hours
notify: NCUA
applies_at_this_tier: No - not a credit union

obligation: Covered telecommunications / Kaspersky article discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-25 (Section 889) and FAR 52.204-23; FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies covered equipment or a Kaspersky covered article
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification for covered telecommunications equipment or services (52.204-25(d)); within 3 business days for a Kaspersky covered article (52.204-23(c)); further report within 10 business days in both cases. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
notify: Contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts or subcontracts
